design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - moving_truck_rentals task 0 (written as the task was designed; every figure below is the output of /tmp/run_0051/moving_truck_rentals/calc_t0.py, which replays the gold writes with the real tools and evaluates each policy's compute with check_compute's own primitives at that write's handling time).

[Step 0 - draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 6, 6]}. Assignment: truck_ext_move_in_rental_waiver (root) 6 factors, truck_ext_move_in_mileage_allowance 6, truck_ext_late_cancellation_fee 4, truck_ext_additional_day_charge 4. Occupied before this task: nothing (first task of the difficulty). Claimed here: those four policies and their tools cancel_truck_reservation_ee0618b8 (owner=user), post_additional_rental_day_charge_add5e32c, apply_move_in_claim_miles_credit_24951572, credit_move_in_rental_waiver_7c9a948d. Left for task 1 (draw: 1 prerequisite, factors [6, 5]): the pickup side of the counter - the first-day rental fee (truck_ext_first_day_rate) and the deposit authorization placed when the renter signs the contract (truck_ext_signing_authorization_hold, owner=user) - a disjoint subject (truck_pickup / truck_deposit_hold) with its own user tool, so task 1 has an independent load-bearing tree.

[Why this is a good test] The caller says only that the free move-in truck was not applied to last week's truck bill. Getting the bill right needs the agent to (1) read the free move-in rules and find that the benefit can be claimed on that contract only when no other open truck contract of hers holds a claim on the same storage unit - and her Sunday 2026-10-11 reservation does; (2) notice that the returned contract started a second rental day that nobody charged, because the mileage allowance waits on every started day being charged; (3) record the claim with the included-miles credit, and only then (4) credit the rental waiver, whose shares read the claimed unit through the contract. Each write is a multi-factor calculation over history (storage ledger counts, contract ledger lines), dates (weekday, booked days, move-in date) and three other products (unit, protect, autopay). Nothing is guessable from tool names; every number comes from policy plus records.

[Problem-tree card] root = truck_ext_move_in_rental_waiver. Edges:
 E1 waiver -> mileage allowance: kind value_input, gate claimed_size (the waiver's claimed-unit reads), form state, prerequisite sentence "The rental waiver is not credited before the truck contract carries the storage-unit claim it is credited for." (negated direction). Four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... before'; waits on a record-visible state (the contract's linked storage unit); names no tool/id/code token; strength = hard requirement, scope = the one contract. Exactly one write of this difficulty sets truck_rentals.linked_rental_id: apply_move_in_claim_miles_credit_24951572 (no other tool writes that field). Opening fact: initial_state.truck_rentals.<C>.linked_rental_id = null (walk-in contract, never linked). Resolved by the agent.
 E2 mileage allowance -> late cancellation fee: kind state_gate, gate truck_rentals.status, form state, sentence "The included-miles credit is not posted until no other reserved, picked-up or returned truck contract of the renter carries a claim on the same storage unit." (negated). Only the renter's cancellation moves a reservation out of reserved status in this difficulty (the no-show is a system transition with no tool), so the sentence + the records (reservation R, status reserved, linked to unit K-214) + the cancellation policy's own rule lead to exactly one action: the renter cancels R. Opening fact: initial_state.truck_rentals.<R>.status = reserved with linked_rental_id = <K-214>. Resolved by the customer through the hand-over tool (owner=user): cancelling a booking is the renter's own act (blueprint summary).
 E3 mileage allowance -> additional-day charge: kind value_input, gate rental_days_charged, form state, sentence "The included-miles credit is fixed only after every rental day the contract started stands charged on the contract." (affirmative). Only post_additional_rental_day_charge_add5e32c posts base rental fee lines at check-in (the first-day line is posted when a contract opens, which already happened). Opening fact: C was picked up 2026-10-02 09:15 and returned 2026-10-03 13:10 (two rental days started) but carries a single base_rental_fee line of quantity 1, so one rental day is charged (initial_state.truck_charges.<first-day line>).
 Topological order: {cancel R, additional day} -> mileage allowance -> waiver; gold uses cancel(9), additional day(11), miles(13), waiver(15). Cancel and additional day are parallel prerequisites of the mileage allowance and touch different contracts (R vs C) and different rows, ids are content hashes of their own arguments, so either order gives the same terminal hash. Directions in the charter: two negated (E1, E2), one affirmative (E3); task 1 adds another affirmative.
 Deletion sensitivity (calc_t0.py skip run): skipping the claim (step 13) moves the waiver from 12.37 to 22.91; skipping the additional day (step 11) moves the mileage credit from 185.13 to 155.43; skipping the cancellation leaves the mileage figure at 185.13 but leaves R reserved with its claim, so the once-per-unit gate on the credit is false and the terminal state differs (R status and fee line) - the state_gate edge bears weight on the gate, as declared.
 user_scenario never names the Sunday booking, a fee, miles or extra days; the booking appears only as a passive reaction after the agent raises it. The tools validate nothing (see tools_do_not_block).

[Base-invariant card] Cancellation (subject truck_reservation_cancelled): governed by truck_evt_cancellation_no_show only; its single gate (free_cancellation_cutoff) applies to truck_charge, so the write carries policy_scope; the free/late split is inherited unchanged: 10 ft free_cancellation_hours_before_pickup = 24; R's pickup is 2026-10-11 09:00 and frozen_time is 2026-10-10 14:20 MST, 18 h 40 m before, so the cancellation is late and the fee computation applies (a cancellation at 2026-10-10 09:00 or earlier would have been free). Additional day (subject truck_return): truck_evt_pricing and truck_evt_late_return, neither with a gate on truck_return -> policy_scope; no late fee arises because C came back before its scheduled return 2026-10-04 09:15. Credits (subject truck_credit): truck_agg_free_move_in_once.once_per_unit (dedup on linked_rental_id over reserved/picked_up/returned/closed contracts - false at the opening because R holds the claim), truck_evt_free_move_in.unit_status_ok (K-214 active, same customer), inside_window (time: pickup 2026-10-02 vs move-in 2026-10-03 + free_move_in_window_days 7 = 2026-10-10 and not earlier than 2026-09-26; counting from the day after the move-in date, last day included; a pickup on 2026-10-11 would fail, 2026-10-10 passes), class_eligible (10 ft: free_move_in_eligible true), truck_evt_breakdown_and_corrections.not_already_credited (the mileage line and the first-day line carry no credit).

[Business-object card] Target contract C (10 ft, PHX-031, returned) for the mileage, additional-day and waiver writes; target reservation R (10 ft, PHX-031, reserved, booked 2026-09-21, pickup Sun 2026-10-11 09:00, return 2026-10-13 09:00, linked to K-214) for the cancellation. Correlation keys: credits reference the exact line credited (mileage line, first-day line); the claim is the storage agreement of her latest storage administrative fee (K-214, admin fee 2026-10-03) - not L-033 (admin fee 2025-07-12). Rows excluded: the hold line and the environmental fee line (stay chargeable), L-033's own ledger except as rent-count evidence.

[Factor card - values are the calc_t0.py output]
 Late cancellation fee (4): fee basis (method) booked 2 days -> the larger of one base_rate_usd 29.95 and the flat 25.00 = 29.95 (baseline flat 25.00 -> 21.09); notice share 1 day -> 0.75 (baseline 1.0 -> 33.69); peak day Sunday -> 1.5 (-> 16.85); tenant courtesy (cross-difficulty unit) existing-tenant tier 0.75 because no active agreement at the reservation's facility PHX-031 moved in within a month and rent was billed within twelve months (-> 33.69). Result 25.27; all-baseline 25.00. Near-miss: K-214 moved in 2026-10-03 but at PHX-027; a careless reader who ignores the facility puts her on the new-tenant tier 0.5 and gets 16.85.
 Additional day (4): last-day share back 13:10 on the day the second day began, within the two booked days, after 12:00 and by 15:00 -> 0.75 day (baseline whole day -> 29.66); additional-day rate source (method) booked two days -> the first-day fee as posted 32.95 (baseline class rate 29.95 -> 20.22); second day began Saturday 2026-10-03 -> 1.2 (-> 18.53); move-in share (multi-source, cross-difficulty unit) K-214 moved in on the return date but at PHX-027, not the pickup facility -> 0.75 (-> 29.66). Result 22.24 (22.24125, no half-cent tie); all-baseline 29.95. Near-miss: the facility of K-214; ignoring it gives the same-facility tier 0.5 and 14.83.
 Mileage allowance (6): claimed unit = latest admin fee -> K-214 5x10 -> 60 miles (-> 170.28); rental days charged (quantities of the base rental fee lines) 2 after the additional day -> +20 (-> 155.43); move-in trip miles (method) pickup one day before move-in -> 10 miles per day of lead = 10 (-> 170.28); Climate Plus -> +10 (-> 170.28); unit at PHX-027, truck from PHX-031, pickup before move-in -> +25 (multi-source; -> 148.50); $5,000 protection plan active (cross-difficulty protect) x1.5 (-> 123.75). Allowance int(125 x 1.5) = 187 < 230 miles charged; credit 187 x 0.99 = 185.13; all-baseline 50 x 0.99 = 49.50. Near-miss: L-033 (5x5 Interior Standard, own insurance) would give 50 miles x1.0 if a reader took her older unit.
 Rental waiver (6): basis (method) two-day booking with a Friday scheduled pickup -> the lower of the posted 32.95 and the class base_rate_usd, 29.95 (-> 13.61); 5x10 -> 0.8 (-> 15.47); first-month promotion on K-214 -> 0.75 (-> 16.50); 13 rent charges in 12 months -> 0.85 (-> 14.56); other facility, pickup before move-in -> 0.9 (multi-source; -> 13.75); no AutoPay ever on K-214 (cross-difficulty autopay; L-033's cancelled authorization is the near-miss: it belongs to another agreement, and counting it as K-214's inactive authorization gives the 0.95 tier and 13.06) -> 0.9 (-> 13.75). The figured waiver is compared with the balance the contract owes when it is credited (ledger reconciliation over C's charge, credit, payment and refund lines: 287.89 charged - 185.13 credited = 102.76), which does not bind. Result 12.37; all-baseline 32.95.
 Every factor's tier rests on seeded rows; no stamp names an outcome.

[Seed design] 2 storage agreements (L-033 since 2025-07-12 with 15 monthly rent charges and payments; K-214 moved in 2026-10-03 with admin fee, discounted first rent 56.00 = 112 x 0.5, payment 85.00), K-214's active $5,000 plan (premium balance 0.00), L-033's AutoPay given 2025-07-12 and revoked 2025-07-30 before any draft, contract C with hold 250.40 (credit card, 10 ft: 150.00 x 1.25 last-minute share + 32.95 first-day fee + 29.95 two-day rental estimate under the signing-hold rule), first-day fee 32.95 (29.95 x 1.1 Friday rate, no other first-day adjustment applies to a walk-in with no unit at PHX-031), mileage 230 x 0.99 = 227.70 posted without included miles because C was not linked at check-in, environmental fee 5.00, balance 265.65; reservation R. Fuel came back full and the truck clean, so no fuel or cleaning obligation is lit; no breakdown, no waiver taken, no additional driver.

[Persona] Brisk, practical voice; volunteers only the surface goal; identity details and truck/unit facts only when asked; the Sunday booking only as a reaction; accepts quoted fees; ends when told the move-in credit is on the bill. The last gold write is that credit.

[Standard solution] find_customers by phone -> verify (DOB + photo ID last four) -> read truck contracts, C's charges, storage agreements and ledger, protection plans, AutoPay -> explain that the Sunday booking holds the unit's claim; renter cancels it with fee 25.27 -> post the additional day 22.24 (service date 2026-10-03, 1 additional day) -> record the claim on C for K-214 and credit 185.13 against the mileage line -> credit the waiver 12.37 against the first-day line.

[Revision log] replay_tasks first failed: empty-string id fields counted as dangling foreign keys and two protection fee rows were read by no action -> empty id fields seeded as null, the unread fee rows dropped (the plan's premium balance 0.00 carries the same fact); re-run: REPLAY OK, figures unchanged (16.85 / 7.19 / 185.13 / 12.37).
[Revision 2] the final check_compute suite rule needs one task with >= 8 reconciled history rows; the waiver's rule already implied that a credit never exceeds what the contract owes, so that cap is now stated in the rule and computed from C's ledger (charges, refunds, credits, payments), lifting task 0's reconciled rows to 8; figures unchanged.
[Manual values gates - task 0] Length: surface goal -> waiver's sentence (claim on the contract) -> mileage allowance's two sentences (no other open claim; every rental day charged) -> cancellation and additional-day computations; breadth: unit, protect and autopay records plus contract ledger and dates. The owner=user tool is the cancellation of her own booking, decided by her on the spot. Persona never names a prerequisite; volunteered facts (truck last week, new unit) are in initial_state. Base gates checked above with boundary dates. No real-world wait. Ladders are stated in full in each rule, tiers disjoint, baselines are the computation documents' standard methods. Draft from visible context agrees with gold.
[Revision 3 - policy-task audit round 2] F-1: the condition of the mileage -> cancellation edge now matches its sentence (no other reserved, picked_up or returned contract carries the unit; closed contracts are admitted). F-2: mislabelled method factors replaced - additional day: the last-day count is now a parameter and a genuine method (additional-day rate source: first-day fee as posted / lower of it and the class rate / class rate) replaces the booked-length share; mileage: protection multiple relabelled parameter, move-in trip miles became the method (flat miles on the move-in date, miles per day of lead for earlier pickups); waiver: the basis switches source (class rate for weekend/Friday longer bookings, a share of the class rate for part-day bookings, the posted fee otherwise). F-3: rental-day miles now read the rental days charged (sum of base rental fee quantities), so all three tiers are reachable. F-6/T0-F2: the courtesy tiers use 'less than one whole calendar month / twelve whole calendar months before the cancellation date' and tier 1 requires the agreement at the reservation's facility. T0-F4: near-misses now exist in the cancellation (K-214 at another facility, 16.85 if counted) and the additional day (same record, 9.88 if counted). T0-O1: the persona ends only when told the truck rental itself is credited (the rental waiver, the last write), without naming any other adjustment. T0-O2: C's hold reseeded to the signing-hold rule (250.40). O-1: rental days beyond the booked days are late-return periods, not additional days. Figures now: 25.27 / 14.83 / 185.13 / 12.37, all recomputed by calc_t0.py.
[Revision 4 - policy-task audit round 3] R2-F1: the waiver's discount sentence and its basis tiers now agree - the part-day and Friday-to-Sunday tiers take the lower of the posted first-day fee and the tariff figure, and the rule states that the waiver is never figured on more than the fee as posted. O-5: an authorization given but no longer active now keeps 0.95 of the waiver (above the 0.9 of a unit that never had AutoPay), and the tenancy share is stated as following from the benefit being an acquisition benefit for new storage customers. R2-O1 (contracted day rate x second-day surcharge) and R2-O2 (vault military floor equals the former-military rate) reviewed and kept, reasons below. No scored value of this task moved (25.27 / 14.83 / 185.13 / 12.37); the AutoPay near-miss figure is now 13.06.
[Accepted observations] R2-O1: a two-day booking is billed its contracted day rate (the first-day fee as posted) for the extra day, and the second-day weekday multiple prices demand on the day actually used; a rental agreement that fixes a day rate and adds a day-of-use surcharge is a published pattern, so both stay. R2-O2: for the vault class, whose own military_discount_pct is 0.00, the active-military tier yields the 0.05 floor, the same figure as a former-military renter - a coherent "at least the former-military rate" floor. O-2 (base measure vs base dedup) and O-3 (subjects outside the blueprint claim list) come from the frozen base and move nothing here.
[Revision 5 - KB audit round 4, source-side notes] The additional-day charge used to land on an exact half-cent (32.95 x 0.5 x 1.2 x 0.75 = 14.8275), where "rounded to the cent once" leaves half-up and half-even apart. The world was moved off the tie rather than the charter changed (the published KB stays a lossless rendering): contract C now came back at 13:10 instead of 11:40, so the last additional day takes the afternoon share 0.75 and the charge is 32.95 x 0.75 x 1.2 x 0.75 = 22.24125 -> 22.24 under any rounding convention. Every other scored value of this task (25.27 / 185.13 / 12.37) has no tie: 25.2703, 185.13 exactly, 12.3723. The return at 13:10 is still within the booked days (scheduled return 2026-10-04 09:15), so no late-return period arises; the waiver's balance cap is now 102.76 and still does not bind. Identity-verification note: gold verifies with date of birth and photo ID last four; an agent that also passes the phone number writes the same verification record (its id is a hash of the customer id, its fields verified/verified_at), so the terminal state is identical - no source change.
[Verification] calc_t0.py output reproduced in computations; gates run per task: check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cache_diff, check_cross_fire (results in the final report of this run). Draft from visible context: with the four policy texts, the tool schemas, the finder outputs and the persona, a reader reaches the same order and numbers; the only judgement calls (which unit is claimed, which lines are credited) are pinned by the latest-admin-fee sentence and by the reference lines named in the rules.
user_scenario: You are Marisol Tavares, a dental hygienist in Scottsdale who moved a load of things into a new Bluegate storage unit last weekend. You are calling on a Saturday afternoon, polite but a little worn out, and you like to get to the point. You open with: "Hi, I rented one of your moving trucks last week for my move-in and the bill still shows the full truck rental. When I signed for my new unit they told me the move-in truck comes free with it, so I'd like that put right on the truck bill." You want whatever is owed to you on that truck bill handled on this call, and you are happy for the agent to make the changes on the bill for you. You only give your details when the agent asks for them: the mobile number on your profile is 6025554731, your date of birth is 1988-04-19, the last four characters of your photo ID are 4096, and if a third detail is wanted your billing ZIP code is 85257. If the agent asks about the truck, you remember picking up a 10 ft truck at the Bluegate lot on Friday morning, October 2, and dropping it back a little after one in the afternoon on Saturday, October 3; you had it booked through Sunday but finished early. If the agent asks about the unit, it is your new 5x10 climate unit K-214, which you signed for on Saturday, October 3, at the other Phoenix Bluegate, the same place where you have kept your small unit L-033 since last summer. If you are asked, you took the $5,000 protection plan on the new unit, you pay that unit in the office, and you never set up AutoPay on it. You do not know how the move-in benefit is worked out, what the miles or days cost, or what the bill should come to, and you say so if asked. If the agent tells you that you still have another truck booking, the one for Sunday, October 11, you are surprised and say you completely forgot about it: you booked it back in September when you thought you would move in later, and you have no use for it now. If the agent then explains that this booking is what stands in the way of the move-in benefit on last week's truck, you tell them you will cancel that Sunday booking yourself, and you accept whatever cancellation fee the agent tells you without arguing; when the agent hands the cancellation over to you, you carry it out on that Sunday booking with the fee amount the agent gives you, and you read back what the confirmation says if asked. You do not bring that booking up on your own. Whatever amounts the agent tells you, you take them as given; if a number sounds odd you simply say you trust them to have it right. You end the call only once the agent tells you that the truck rental itself has been credited on last week's truck bill; then you thank them and hang up.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The cancellation (writes reservation R and a fee line on R) and the additional-day charge (writes a line on C and C's balance) are parallel prerequisites of the mileage allowance; they touch disjoint rows, their ids hash only their own arguments, and neither reads the other, so cancel-then-charge and charge-then-cancel give the same terminal hash and the same 185.13 / 12.37. The mileage allowance must precede the waiver (the waiver reads the link it writes) and follows both, as the two prerequisite sentences of the mileage policy state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without step 13 the contract has no linked unit: the waiver evaluates to 22.91 instead of 12.37, and C keeps an empty linked_rental_id and no mileage credit line.

Without step 9 R stays reserved with K-214's claim: the once-per-unit gate of the included-miles credit is false, the terminal state lacks R's cancelled status and its 25.27 fee line, and a credit posted anyway would duplicate the claim (state_gate; the computed figure itself stays 185.13).
Without step 11 C carries one rental day charged: rental-day miles 0, allowance int(105 x 1.5) = 157, credit 155.43 instead of 185.13, and the 22.24 line is missing.
